GALERKIN APPROXIMATION OF A SHIELDED
DOUBLE-SIDED MICROSTRIP LINE WITH BOUNDARY
SINGULARITIES
Yulia V. Rassokhina∗, Vladimir G. Krizhanovski†, Vasyl F. Komarov‡
Abstract.
We provide a mathematical and numerical analysis for solving an eigenvalue boundary
value problems (Dirichlet and Neumann) for Helmholtz operator, which describes a regular
shielded double-sided microstrip transmission line problem. The paper presents a new
adapted method for numerical calculation of dispersion characteristics of this problem,
and, in particular, balanced microstrip line problem. The boundary value problem for
a regular planar transmission line is solved in a rigorous formulation considering the
singularity of the behavior of the current density at the edges of the microstrips. The
method of discretization by Galerkin approximations of the boundary value problem using
an additional basis from Chebyshev polynomials of the 1st and 2nd kind was adapted for
the case of a doubly connected domain (two electrodynamically coupled microstrip lines).
In an explicit form, the matrix elements for the system of linear algebraic equations
were obtained, the solution algorithm of which was implemented in a high-performance
computing environment. The dispersion characteristics of a double-sided microstrip and
balanced transmission line made on the RO3010 substrate material were calculated using
the developed algorithm. As an example of using the obtained dispersion characteristics,
a circuit was designed and the scattering characteristics of tapered transition with an
exponential profile from a double-sided microstrip with a characteristic impedance Z0 =
50 Ohm to a balanced transmission line with a impedance of Z0 = 100 Ohm were obtained.
According to the results of the analysis of exponential transitions with exponents n =
0.707 and n = 1.0 in the function of the strip width versus the longitudinal coordinate,
the reflection coefficient is below |Γ| < 0.1.
Key words: Galerkin approximations, eigenvalues for Helmholtz operator, boundary
value problem, boundary singularities, double-sided microstrip line problem, dispersion
characteristics, Chebyshev polynomials.
Mathematics Subject Classification MSC2020: 35J05, 35J25.

A double-sided microstrip transmission line (broadside-coupled strip) is an
important part of many microwave frequency range devices: baluns, filters, cou-
plers, antennas [11]– [20]. To design devices, both the symmetrical structure of
this transmission line, when w1 = w2 (the so-called balanced microstrip line) and
the asymmetrical (microstrip) structure, when w1 ̸= w2, are used.
A shielded structure symmetrical with respect to the plane x = 0 with two
stripline transmission lines of width w1 and w2, which are located on opposite
sides of one dielectric substrate of thickness h with dielectric permittivity εr,
Fig. 1.1 is considered. The fundamental mode of both, the usual microstrip and
balanced transmission line, corresponds to symmetry with a magnetic wall of the
plane x = 0.
Double-sided microstrip lines are an essential part of structures connecting
different types of transmission lines and provide broadband impedance transfor-
mation, filters, transitions and antennas [11]– [16].
The basic construction of
balanced circuits using double-sided microstrip lines is the transition from a mi-
crostrip transmission line to a balanced line, which is traditionally implemented
using smooth tapered transition [5], [6] and [16]. In this case, both the upper and
lower strips can have a smooth tapered profile. The most widely known transi-
tion profiles are the exponential and Klopfenstein profiles [16], which are included
in the element database of many microwave circuit analysis programs. We con-
sider and analyze the model, described before. This model can be constructed
as boundary value problem for the Helmholtz’s operator eigenvalues of a regular
shielded double-sided microstrip transmission line with a symmetrical location of

3. Results of numerical calculations of dispersion characteristics
The algorithm for analyzing a double-sided microstrip line was implemented
in the computing environment. The eigenvalues χe(o) (the slow-wave factor) were
found by the secant method, and the system of linear algebraic equations was
solved by the Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting.
Numerical calculations of dispersion characteristics in the frequency range
from 1.0 to 6.0 GHz were performed in high-performance computing environment
under conditions of truncation of Fourier series (2.6)–(2.7) to N = 300, and series
of Chebyshev polynomials (2.8)–(2.9) to K = 5.
Under these conditions, the
accuracy of the slow-wave factor calculation is not worse than ε = 10−3. The
screen parameters in the calculations were chosen as follows (in mm): A = 15.0,
b1 = b2 = 15.0.
Fig. 3.1 shows the results of calculations of the dispersion characteristics of
a double-sided microstrip transmission line with the following parameter values:
substrate RO3010 εr = 10.2, h = 1.27 mm, width of the upper strip is (in mm)
w1 = 1.22, and lower strip is w2 = 9.0. The operating mode of a double-sided
microstrip transmission line is an odd wave with a wave impedance Z1,odd = 50
Ohm.
Fig. 3.2 shows the results of calculations of the dispersion characteristics of a
balanced microstrip transmission line with width w1 = w2 = 0.552 mm with a
characteristic impedance of Z1,odd = 100 Ohm.
4. Tapered transition
As it has been mentioned before, double-sided microstrip lines are an essential
part of structures connecting different types of transmission lines and provide
broadband impedance transformation, filters, transitions and antennas [11]– [16].
The basic construction of balanced circuits using double-sided microstrip lines is
the transition from a microstrip transmission line to a balanced line, which is
traditionally implemented using smooth tapered transition [5], [6] and [16]. In
this case, both the upper and lower strips can have a smooth tapered profile.
The most widely known transition profiles are the exponential and Klopfenstein
profiles [16], which are included in the element database of many microwave circuit
analysis programs.

mission line to a balanced line with an exponential profile. The general formula
for the strip width as a function of the normalized longitudinal coordinate z for

5. Conclusions
The boundary value problem for the eigenwaves of a regular shielded double-
sided microstrip transmission line with a symmetrical location of strips was con-
sidered. The boundary value problem is solved by the Galerkin method using an
additional basis for describing the current density on the strips, which considers
the singularity of the field at the edges.
The algorithm is implemented in computing environment. As an example of
calculation, the dispersion characteristics of a double-sided microstrip line with a
characteristic impedance of odd mode Zodd = 50 Ohm and a balanced microstrip
line with a characteristic impedance of Zodd = 100 Ohm on the RO3010 substrate
material are given.

Abstract: We provide a mathematical and numerical analysis for solving an eigenvalue boundary value problems (Dirichlet and Neumann) for Helmholtz operator, which describes a regular shielded double-sided microstrip transmission line problem. The paper presents a new adapted method for numerical calculation of dispersion characteristics of this problem, and, in particular, balanced microstrip line problem. The boundary value problem for a regular planar transmission line is solved in a rigorous formulation considering the singularity of the behavior of the current density at the edges of the microstrips. The method of discretization by Galerkin approximations of the boundary value problem using an additional basis from Chebyshev polynomials of the 1st and 2nd kind was adapted for the case of a doubly connected domain (two electrodynamically coupled microstrip lines). In an explicit form, the matrix elements for the system of linear algebraic equations were obtained, the solution algorithm of which was implemented in a high-performance computing environment. The dispersion characteristics of a double-sided microstrip and balanced transmission line made on the RO3010 substrate material were calculated using the developed algorithm. As an example of using the obtained dispersion characteristics, a circuit was designed and the scattering characteristics of tapered transition with an exponential profile from a double-sided microstrip with a characteristic impedance Z0 = 50 Ohm to a balanced transmission line with a impedance of Z0 = 100 Ohm were obtained. According to the results of the analysis of exponential transitions with exponents n = 0.707 and n = 1.0 in the function of the strip width versus the longitudinal coordinate, the reflection coefficient is below |Γ| < 0.1.
